children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw two lines $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ through $O$ such that, when triangle $ABC$ is reflected in $\ell_1$ and its image is reflected in $\ell_2$, the final result is triangle $A'B'C'$.

answer.short: One possible construction is shown: $\ell_1$ slopes upwards to the right at $45^{\circ}$ to the horizontal, and $\ell_2$ is vertical. Reflect in $\ell_1$ first, then in $\ell_2$.
answer.worked: Draw a vertical line $\ell_2$ through $O$ and a line $\ell_1$ through $O$ sloping upwards to the right at $45^{\circ}$ to the horizontal. Reflect each vertex of $ABC$ in $\ell_1$, placing its image at the same perpendicular distance on the other side. Join these vertices to form the intermediate triangle. Reflect its vertices in $\ell_2$ in the same way; the resulting triangle coincides with $A'B'C'$.

spec.sourceRegion: Challenge exercise 5a; teacher PDF page 59, upper-right answer
spec.description: Complete construction with the two original triangles, a dotted intermediate reflected triangle, dashed reflection axes through O and the 45-degree angle. Double primes identify the intermediate triangle, following the teacher figure.
spec.mathematics: Reflection first in the line at 45 degrees to the horizontal and then in the vertical line gives a 90-degree anticlockwise rotation about O.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only: both axes, intermediate image and angle are supplied.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Measure the acute angle between lines $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$.

answer.worked: Place the protractor centre at $O$ and align its baseline with one reflection axis. Read the acute angle to the other axis: $45^{\circ}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Is there only one choice for the position of lines $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$?

answer.short:
No. There are many possible pairs of axes through $O$.

The acute angle must be $45^{\circ}$, with the reflections ordered to produce the anticlockwise rotation.
answer.worked: Both axes can be turned together about $O$ while keeping the directed angle from $\ell_1$ to $\ell_2$ equal to $45^{\circ}$ anticlockwise. The two reflections still produce the given $90^{\circ}$ anticlockwise rotation, so there are many choices.
